sources.quote: Google's own guidance is to change one major thing at a time where practical
sources.title: Site Moves and Migrations | Google Search Central | Documentation | Google for Developers
sources.evidence: Plan your changes to your site one after the other, not everything at the same time. We recommend not implementing other major changes when you're moving your content to a new location, like large-scale content, URL structure, or navigational updates. Changing too much at once may confuse users and search engines.

sources.quote: Use Search Console's Links report or a tool like Ahrefs to list every page with external links
sources.title: Links report - Search Console Help
sources.evidence: The Links report allows you to see who links to you the most, your top-linked pages, and more. External links: Top linked pages show which of your pages have the most backlinks from other sites. You can export your link data as a CSV file or a Google Sheet.

sources.quote: Target Largest Contentful Paint under 2.5 seconds
sources.title: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) | Articles | web.dev
sources.evidence: To provide a good user experience, sites should strive to have Largest Contentful Paint of 2.5 seconds or less. To ensure you're hitting this target for most of your users, a good threshold to measure is the 75th percentile of page loads, segmented across mobile and desktop devices.

sources.quote: Speed is a ranking factor and a conversion factor
sources.title: Understanding Core Web Vitals and Google search results | Google Search Central | Documentation | Google for Developers
sources.evidence: Core Web Vitals is a set of metrics that measure real-world user experience for loading performance, interactivity, and visual stability of the page. Core Web Vitals are used by our ranking systems. Good stats within the Core Web Vitals report in Search Console don't guarantee good rankings.

sources.quote: Password-protect the staging site or use noindex
sources.title: Block Search Indexing with noindex | Google Search Central | Documentation | Google for Developers
sources.evidence: robots.txt is not a mechanism for keeping a web page out of Google. To keep a web page out of Google, block indexing with noindex or password-protect the page. The noindex rule is set with either a meta tag or HTTP response header; when Googlebot crawls that page and extracts the tag or header, Google will drop that page entirely from Google Search results.

sources.quote: No chains (A to B to C), no loops, no 302 temporary redirects
sources.title: Redirects and Google Search | Google Search Central | Documentation | Google for Developers
sources.evidence: Googlebot can follow up to 10 hops in a chain of multiple redirects; Google advises redirecting to the final destination directly, and if not possible, keep the number of redirects in the chain low, ideally no more than 3 and fewer than 5. Permanent redirects (301 and 308) signal to Google to display the new target URL in search results, while temporary redirects (302/303/307) maintain the source page in results. If you need to change the URL of a page as it is shown in search engine results, use a permanent server-side redirect whenever possible.

sources.quote: use Search Console's Change of Address tool
sources.title: Change of Address tool - Search Console Help
sources.evidence: The Change of Address tool is used when you move your website from one domain or subdomain to another. When you file a change of address request using Search Console, it tells Google to emphasize crawling and indexing your new site over crawling your old site, and forwards various signals from the old site to the new site. These actions continue for 180 days. Maintain the redirects for at least 180 days—longer if you still see any traffic to them from Google Search.
